what_happened.line: The Charter Review Committee adopted an operating rule that major items need a supermajority of six of its nine members; the recorded vote was not audible.
Members volunteered to contact specific elected and appointed town boards about the charter.
A blast email to all departments and committees will announce the charter review.
A member volunteered to draft a press release for the next paper.
Two or three members were asked to research open versus representative town meeting; the form of town meeting, town manager duties and department heads were left unresolved.

why_it_matters: Any major change to the town charter, which sets how Town Meeting, the town manager and departments are organized, will need six of nine committee members before it moves on, so small majorities cannot carry it.
The open versus representative town meeting question, if it advances, would change how residents take part in voting on town budgets and bylaws.
watch_next: The press release and the blast email to departments and committees, which are the first steps for residents and boards to give input.
The committee's research on open versus representative town meeting.
